title: Gala and Fundraiser Planning Kit
subtitle: For nonprofit teams and volunteer committees planning a gala, benefit dinner, or auction fundraiser.
intro: A fundraiser is a party with a purpose, and the details decide how much money you raise. This kit covers your committee, timeline, sponsorship tiers, auction planning, run of show, budget, volunteer roles, and donor follow-up. Use it to keep your team organized and your guests generous.

sections.heading: Committee Roles and Timeline
sections.note: Start 9 to 12 months out for a large gala. Smaller benefits can compress this to 4 to 6 months. Book a date early, since spring and fall Chicago calendars fill quickly.

tasks: Recruit a chair or co-chairs and a committee of 6 to 12 people.
Set a fundraising goal and a net revenue target after expenses.
Choose the event theme, format, and approximate guest count.
Pick the date and avoid conflicts with other major Chicago-area galas and holidays.
Tour and book the venue.
Draft the budget and get board approval.
Create the sponsorship packages and begin outreach to sponsors.
Recruit an honoree, keynote speaker, or emcee.
Book the caterer, DJ or band, photographer, and AV team.
Reserve rentals: tables, chairs, linens, glassware, staging, lighting, and tent if needed.
Start collecting auction items and experiences.
Set up an online ticketing and donation platform.
Send save-the-dates to your donor list.
Confirm sponsor commitments and logos for printed materials.
Plan the program, run of show, and appeal moment.
Order invitations and sponsor recognition signage.
Choose the auction method: silent, live, mobile bidding, or all three.
Book auctioneer if holding a live auction.
Send formal invitations with ticket and table purchase options.
Follow up personally with top donors and sponsors.
Finalize auction items and write descriptions.
Design the program book and ads.
Confirm the menu and dietary tracking.
Draft the seating plan strategy for sponsors, board members, and honorees.
Send reminder emails and texts to unregistered supporters.
Finalize the guest list and table assignments.
Print bid sheets, signage, and programs.
Test the mobile bidding platform and payment processing.
Confirm volunteer shifts and send training materials.
Share the run of show with every vendor and speaker.
Confirm final headcount with the caterer and rental company.
Prepare the guest check-in list and name badges.
Pack the day-of kit and cash box.
Hold a volunteer briefing.
Check the forecast and finalize the coat check and weather plan.
Pre-write thank-you messages for sponsors and donors.
Inspect the rental delivery and count tables, chairs, linens, and glassware.
Set up auction tables, bid sheets, and display items.
Test microphones, projector, and mobile bidding.
Brief volunteers and staff at the venue.
Greet sponsors and VIP guests first.
Keep the program on time and the appeal moment short and powerful.
Schedule the rental pickup and count items returned.
Pay winning bidders' receipts and distribute auction items.
Send thank-you messages to everyone within 48 hours.
Reconcile revenue and expenses within two weeks.
Hold a committee debrief and document lessons learned.

sections.heading: Sponsorship Tiers
sections.note: Sample structure only. The amounts are illustrations. Set your own levels based on your donor base and goals.
rows: Naming rights, two reserved tables, speaking moment, logo on all materials, full-page program ad
Reserved table of 10, logo on signage and website, half-page ad, social media recognition
Reserved table of 10, logo on signage, quarter-page ad, mention in the program
Five tickets, name on signage, name in the program
Two tickets, name in the program
Seats for 8 or 10 guests, name on the table, recognition in the program
Logo or name on signage, acknowledgment in the program, tax receipt where eligible

groups.title: Procuring items
items: Set a target number of items based on guest count, with roughly one item for every 4 to 5 guests.
Ask local businesses, board members, and donors for experiences and goods.
Prioritize unique experiences, travel, and exclusive access over generic gift baskets.
Collect donation letters for tax purposes.
Record the fair market value of each item.
Photograph each item and write a short description.

groups.title: Silent auction setup
items: Set a starting bid at about 40 to 50 percent of retail value.
Set bid increments and a buy-it-now option for popular items.
Arrange tables with linens at the height guests can easily read.
Print bid sheets and place pens at every table.
Number each item and match the bid sheet.
Set up mobile bidding with a clear link or QR code.
Choose a closing time and announce it multiple times.

groups.title: Live auction
items: Choose five to ten high-value items for the live auction.
Hire a professional auctioneer or a charismatic volunteer.
Rehearse the order of items and the opening bids.
Prepare a fund-a-need appeal tied to a specific outcome.
Assign spotters to watch the room and call bids.
Build in time for the appeal after dinner while guests are attentive.

groups.title: Checkout
items: Set up a checkout table near the exit with trained staff.
Print or send receipts to winning bidders.
Accept credit cards, mobile payments, and checks.
Match winning bidders with items and arrange pickup or shipping.
Keep a record of unsold items to reuse next year.

sections.note: Sample for a 5:30 pm to 10:30 pm seated gala. Adjust to your venue and program.

sections.heading: Gala Budget Split
sections.note: A typical starting point. Aim for the event to raise much more than it costs. Chicago-area venue and catering costs vary widely.

lines.tip: Negotiate nonprofit rates and ask what is included with the venue fee.
Ask for a nonprofit discount and confirm service charge and gratuity.
Include microphones, projection, lighting, and a technician.
Use sponsor ads to offset the cost of the program book.
Mobile bidding platforms charge a fee or a percentage.
Email and social media reach your donors for less.
Valet and security are often required in downtown venues.
Hold this until the event is over.

sections.heading: Volunteer Roles
sections.note: Assign each role a lead and a backup. Brief everyone one week before.

groups.title: Before doors open
items: Setup crew: place tables, chairs, linens, table numbers, and centerpieces.
Signage lead: place directional signs, sponsor signs, and menu cards.
Auction setup lead: arrange items, bid sheets, and descriptions.
AV liaison: connect with the AV team and run the slides.
Vendor greeter: meet each vendor at the loading dock.

groups.title: During the event
items: Check-in greeters: welcome guests, find names, hand out badges and bid numbers.
Coat check attendants: manage coats and bags, especially from November to March.
Auction spotters: call out bids in the live auction.
Checkout team: process payments and hand out items.
Table hosts: help guests find seats and introduce people.
Photographer liaison: point out sponsors, honorees, and key moments.
Floater: answer questions and fix problems fast.

groups.title: After the event
items: Pack up auction items and unsold goods.
Collect centerpieces, signs, and decor.
Count rental items and stack them for pickup.
Gather lost-and-found items.
Take out the trash and leave the room clean.

groups.title: Within 48 hours
items: Send a thank-you email to every guest, sponsor, and volunteer.
Post photos and a short thank-you on social media.
Send tax receipts for gifts and ticket purchases.
Share the preliminary fundraising total.

groups.title: Within 2 weeks
items: Call or write personal notes to top donors and sponsors.
Send a handwritten note to the honoree and keynote speaker.
Share a short impact story showing how funds will be used.
Update the donor database with every gift and bid.
Reconcile revenue and expenses.

groups.title: Within 3 months
items: Send a progress update to donors showing results.
Invite sponsors to a debrief or renew early.
Survey guests about the event experience.
Document lessons learned and update the playbook.
Save the date for next year's event.
